title: Export deploy metadata for incident-bot (service/version/rollout phase + canary status)
author: Connor O'Brien
release_notes: Internal-only: adds deploy metadata export endpoint + event stream hook used by incident-bot diagnostics cards. No customer-facing behavior change.
description: Context: Incident-bot v2 needs consistent “recent deploy context” during the first 5 minutes of an incident (service, image SHA, rollout phase, canary results, links). Today responders manually cross-reference Spinnaker/Argo + GitHub + our internal service registry, which increases MTTR (see #incidents thread 1739058123 and postmortem 2025-02-07 hosted API 503s). This PR adds a small internal export surface in the redwood control plane so incident-bot (and later Console) can query deploy metadata in a stable, machine-readable format. What’s in this PR: (1) New internal endpoint `GET /internal/deploy-metadata/recent` backed by the deploy controller’s rollout state store. Supports filters: `service`, `region`, `environment`, `limit`, and optional `since` (RFC3339). Response includes: service name (canonical registry key), image tag + image SHA, rollout phase (canary|ramp|full|rollback), rollout id, started_at, last_updated_at, and canary health summary (pass/fail/unknown + gate names). (2) Optional event stream emitter (`DeployMetadataExported`) behind a flag for consumers that prefer push (incident-bot currently will poll; event stream is for follow-up work to reduce query load). (3) Normalization logic to join rollout records to the canonical service registry (fixes “missing service mapping” issues seen in eng-releases 1740086015). (4) Guardrails: endpoint is restricted to service identities with `deploy-metadata:read` scope; response excludes tenant/customer identifiers by design; adds request logging with request_id + caller identity for auditability (detailed audit event wiring is handled in PR-29133). (5) Documentation: internal README for the schema, examples, and stability/versioning notes (`v1` schema with additive-only promise). Notes/decisions: The endpoint is intentionally not tenant-scoped; incident-bot uses it to show “what changed recently in this service/region” independent of tenant. If/when we need tenant-correlation, that should happen in the incident-bot telemetry/config collectors where we have stronger redaction/audit controls. The canary status is derived from the deploy controller’s gate results. When gates aren’t configured, canary_health will be `unknown` rather than failing the request. Rollout phase mapping is based on controller state machine; see `RolloutPhaseMapper` notes in code. Testing: Unit tests cover phase mapping, schema serialization, and service-registry join edge cases (unknown service -> omitted record + metric). Integration test spins up controller + registry fakes and exercises `GET /internal/deploy-metadata/recent?service=hosted-api&region=us-east-1`. Metrics: Adds `deploy_metadata_export_requests_total{status,caller}` and `deploy_metadata_export_join_failures_total{reason}` plus request duration histogram. Rollout: Endpoint is shipped dark behind `deploy_metadata_export_enabled` (default false). Release eng will enable in staging, then prod for incident-bot service identity only. Follow-ups (not in this PR): (a) add Console deep-link generator into response (owned by Chloe), (b) wire audit events to central SIEM (PR-29133), (c) incident-bot card rendering + link-out (incident-bot repo PR-1842).

conversation: Miles Thornton (review): Can we guarantee the service naming matches what incident-bot expects? We’ve had incidents where deploy events used a display name and responders couldn’t correlate.

Connor O'Brien (author): Yep — this uses the canonical service registry key (`service_registry_id`). If the rollout record can’t be joined, we drop it and emit `deploy_metadata_export_join_failures_total{reason="unknown_service"}` so we can catch drift. Added an example to the docs as well.

Sahana Iyer (review): Request: keep the response stable. Can we version the schema and promise additive changes only? Also please ensure we don’t accidentally include tenant/environment variables from the deploy spec.

Connor O'Brien (author): Added `schema_version: "v1"` to the response and documented additive-only promise. The handler uses a dedicated DTO that only includes the allowlisted fields; we don’t serialize the underlying deploy spec. Also added a unit test asserting no `tenant_id`-like keys exist in JSON.
Rafael Mendes (review): On failure modes: if the deploy controller store is degraded during an incident, we need fast timeouts. What are the defaults?

Connor O'Brien (author): Good call. Set handler timeout to 750ms and hard cap to `limit<=20`. If store query exceeds timeout, we return 200 with `partial=true` and `errors=["timeout_querying_rollout_store"]` (incident-bot will render the card with a warning + links).
Ethan Park (review): Authz: please ensure this is service-identity only and not user sessions. Also avoid making it accessible via the general internal gateway without scopes.

Connor O'Brien (author): Implemented `requireServiceIdentity()` middleware + scope check `deploy-metadata:read`. User sessions will get 403. Route is under internal service mesh only (no public gateway).
Miles Thornton (review): Can we add a quick example response for the bot team to code against?
Connor O'Brien (author): Added to docs/internal/deploy-metadata-export.md with fields: service, region, rollout_phase, canary_health, image_sha, started_at, rollout_id.
Sahana Iyer (review): Approving once CI is green.
System: CI was failing: integration-tests (control-plane) — fail (flaky clock dependency).
Connor O'Brien (author): Fixed by injecting a fake clock into the handler test; reran CI.
Miles Thornton (review): Approved — bot team can start integrating.
